messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: hotfix branch protocol
parts:
Ben: I'm trying to ask you the right thing to do this
time before we do it all wrong again.

I want to create a hotfix for the softmax memory leak
(I'm in the airport killing time and this seemed mindless
enough).

I followed our developer process wiki and created a

hotfix/v2.1.1

branch from the most recent master. Then the wiki had me
branch again from there to:

bugfix/issue-472-softmax-leak

I pushed the bugfix branch following instructions, but I
don't see it on GitHub.

Is this the right thing to do or am I doing something wrong?

If the wiki instructions aren't right, can you tell me what
they should be?

Thanks.

- Bob

It doesn't do any harm, but there didn't need to be two branches. You could have just branched hotfix/issue-472-softmax-leak from master.

I pushed the bugfix branch following instructions, but I
don't see it on GitHub.

I see it

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/tree/bugfix/issue-472-softmax-leak

That is basically right. So merge that into develop and also merge it into master and call it a new release.
 
Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: hotfix pull request target?  granularity of patch releases?
parts:
On Wednesday, January 1, 2014 5:11:32 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I branched

   * hotfix/v2.1.1                  from  master

then

   * bugfix/issue-472-softmax-leak  from  hotfix/v2.1.1

I don't think we want to roll out a new release just for this fix,

In that case, it should be considered a fix rather than a hotfix and should have been branched from and merged into develop. But it is okay, since you most likely can just merge it into develop via the normal procedures and the fact that it was branched from master is mostly irrelevant.

so
I think the target branch for the pull request should be hotfix/v2.1.1.  

QUESTION 1:  Should we do a new patch release (v2.1.1 is next)
for each bug fix?

Iff it is sufficiently major. Since softmax is pretty widely used, I don't think anyone would oppose a new release just for this bug. But it is not as if it was something that was affecting everyone (such as getting the variance wrong), which should have warranted a hotfix release.

QUESTION 2:  Is merging into hotfix/v2.1.1 kosher GitFlow?  If not,
how should I do it?

It is more that it would rarely, if ever, be necessary. If you don't want to do a new release because of this bug, then just merge into develop. Then there is no need to merge into that branch and you can throw it away.

Ben

Doesn't that depend on how we want to treat releases?
I was planning to put all the bug fixes on the hotfix branch
and then release occassionally, and more occassionally release
2.(x+1).0 branches from develop.

Well, the idea of medium-level bugs is a conceptual addition to the gitflow workflow, which only distinguishes release-critical commits from other commits. If we accumulate enough medium-level bug fixes to collectively justify a release and there are a few new features that have already been committed, then I don't see what is the point of releasing with only the medium-level bug fixes and not the new features. So, I think you could just push it all into develop and push a commit into master if you think it justifies a new release.

I also think it'd be nice to give users something to branch
from.  I don't mind dropping things into master --- I mainly
just don't want to spam our users with continual patches.

I wouldn't mind tagging a 2.1.1 branch, and just not announcing
it.  And letting RStan and PyStan and CmdStan catch up whenever
convenient.

The thing about a release-critical bug it that it shouldn't really require any catchup, just a rebuild of the RStan and PyStan packages with the new master branch of Stan.

Ben
